title: Wilmot farmland crop destruction and Region service approvals
subtitle: Paramedic station, downtown waste collection, Benton–Frederick bike lanes, airport fees, new auditor, accessible taxi review
overview: Regional Council responded to the plowing under of a corn crop on a 160-acre Wilmot farm bought for an industrial land strategy. Council approved a motion requiring a public report within four weeks, a harvest assessment before any action on future farms, and advance notice to Council of work on those lands {{vote:m9}}. Several delegates, including farming organizations, urged Council to go further and halt the land assembly.

Council also approved a Paramedic Services station at the former Kinsmen Children's Centre site in Cambridge with debenture authority {{vote:m8}}, a new downtown waste collection model for businesses and institutions {{vote:m13}}, and a two-lane layout with painted bike lanes on Benton and Frederick streets. It appointed KPMG as external auditor for five years {{vote:m10}} and set new airport fees from October 1, 2024 {{vote:m15}}.

Council also asked staff to study a centralized accessible taxi dispatch model {{vote:m19}}. Delegations also raised the closure of supervised consumption sites, conditions at the 100 Victoria Street encampment, and signage at the Hidden Valley weir. Council extended its meeting past 11 p.m. {{vote:m16}}.

decisions.item: Wilmot farm crop and Benton–Frederick lanes
decisions.detail: Council committed to a public report on the crop destruction, a harvest assessment before action on future farms and advance notice of work, and approved reducing Benton and Frederick streets to two lanes with painted bike lanes {{vote:m9}}.
Council supported using the former Kinsmen Children's Centre property in Cambridge for a Paramedic Services station and approved debenture authority of $12,600,000 over up to 20 years {{vote:m8}}.

decisions.item: Downtown waste collection and Cambridge rail
decisions.detail: Council approved Region-funded automated cart collection for downtown businesses and institutions, starting March 2, 2026 under the Emterra contract, and endorsed the Cambridge to Union rail study {{vote:m13}}.
Council approved the proposed operating model with a maximum of 66 residents and required community consultation and a further report before any changes {{vote:m7}}.
Council appointed KPMG LLP as the Region's external auditor for 2024 to 2028 at $944,790 plus taxes {{vote:m10}}.

decisions.item: Airport fees, Flair agreement and land exchange
decisions.detail: Council raised airport passenger and parking fees from October 1, 2024, approved a new Flair Airlines agreement, and authorized a memorandum of understanding for a land exchange on Erb Street West {{vote:m15}}.
Council approved pre-budget vehicle and ambulance purchases, tourism and cultural funding, and up to $200,000 toward a June 2025 esports event {{vote:m14}}.
Council directed staff to study Calgary's centralized wheelchair-accessible dispatch and plan a Taxi By-law review, reporting by March 2025 {{vote:m19}}.

debate: Farming delegates said farmland is non-renewable, that plowing the corn contradicted the Region's Strategic Plan, and that the crop could have been donated. Some urged ending the land assembly and boundary expansions, and asked for an inventory of how farmland is used and owned.

Council members supporting the farmland motion thanked delegates, while one delegate said the motion did not go far enough. One councillor asked about the inventory request and a delegate described it as covering ownership, intended use and non-farm uses such as aggregate extraction.

On the paramedic station, one councillor voted against, supporting a new station but arguing the report did not show enough due diligence on housing, childcare or a Cambridge Fire partnership, and objecting to a single-use facility during a housing crisis.

Delegates on homelessness and drug policy described unsafe encampment conditions and the lack of lighting. They warned that closing consumption and treatment sites would cost lives, and called for safe supply funding and advocacy with the province.
A delegate said signs at the Hidden Valley weir are broken or blocked and asked for urgent upgrades and transparency on a staff report. A councillor said the Region would follow up.
